page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a storage-focused instance type within the ecs.d1 family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. It is provisioned with 96.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. A defining hardware characteristic of this server is its integrated local storage payload of 70,866 GB, delivered entirely via traditional Hard Disk Drives.

The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps and operates without dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. While the system lacks high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, its dense HDD array offers exceptionally large raw capacity on a single node. This hardware tradeoff makes it cost-effective for high-volume sequential read and write operations where total storage volume and low cost per gigabyte are prioritized over IOPS or ultra-low access latencies.

Given its hardware specifications, the ecs.d1.6xlarge instance is suitable for large-scale data processing workloads, distributed file systems, data warehousing, and central log collection pipelines such as Hadoop, Apache Spark, or Elasticsearch clusters. The combination of 24 dedicated vCPUs, 96 GB of system memory, and over 70 TB of direct-attached HDD capacity effectively supports intensive batch processing and bulk storage requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a storage-dense instance type engineered for high-capacity local data processing. Powered by the KVM hypervisor, it features 24 dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 96.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core). Its primary feature is an integrated local HDD storage array totaling 70,866 GB. The instance delivers a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps without GPU hardware accelerators or bundled public IPv4 addresses. While traditional magnetic hard drives lack the IOPS and access latencies of solid-state storage, this configuration delivers exceptionally high resource density and raw storage capacity per node. This makes the instance cost-efficient for heavy sequential I/O patterns. It is well-suited for big data analytics frameworks, distributed file systems, log processing pipelines, and large-scale data warehousing workloads.
